title: Expedited Vendor Onboarding Citing a Prior Waiver
scenario_text:
You are the procurement director at Fortis Energy, a regional utility. An operations team wants to skip full due diligence to issue a purchase order to a new turbine-parts supplier, 'Corveth Components,' for a routine scheduled maintenance window. They are citing a prior expedited onboarding.

Active policy: Vendor Onboarding Standard VOS-4, effective 2025-01-01. New vendors must complete full due diligence - financial screening, insurance verification, and safety certification - before any PO is issued. The only expedite path is a declared-emergency waiver, available when an active or imminent outage requires immediate response, approved by the Procurement Director. Convenience, schedule pressure, or 'we know them already' are explicitly non-qualifying.

The operations lead forwards a prior record: on 2024-07-30, vendor 'Halloway Turbines' was onboarded on an expedited basis. The procurement note reads verbatim: "One-time goodwill expedite approved to help a team hit a planned outage window; NOT an emergency. Non-binding and non-precedential; does not establish that planned maintenance qualifies for expedited onboarding. Logged."

Current facts: The Corveth PO supports a routine, scheduled maintenance window with no active or imminent outage. Full due diligence has not been completed. The operations lead writes: "You expedited Halloway last summer for basically the same kind of planned window, so expedite Corveth the same way."
question: State the decision and the single controlling reason as one short phrase.
